comparability: These accounts post about different things, to different audiences, in very different amounts. Read each account’s plays and likes against its own median, not as a league table.

findings.title: Posting frequency split the {{w.p.readable}} readable accounts into two groups
findings.text: {{a.vit.brand}} published {{a.vit.posts_in_window}} posts and {{a.sig.brand}} {{a.sig.posts_in_window}} in the window. {{a.spa.brand}} published {{a.spa.posts_in_window}} and {{a.las.brand}} {{a.las.posts_in_window}}, although {{a.las.brand}} has the largest following of the readable accounts ({{a.las.followers}}). Denominator: all {{p.posts_all}} posts on the {{w.p.readable}} readable feeds in the window.

findings.title: More reels did not mean more plays per reel
findings.text: {{a.vit.brand}} published {{a.vit.reels}} reels with a median of {{a.vit.median_plays}} recorded plays each; {{a.sig.brand}} published {{a.sig.reels}} with a median of {{a.sig.median_plays}}, about {{r.sig.vit.median_plays}} times higher. Denominator: own reels with a recorded play count, {{a.vit.reels_with_plays}} and {{a.sig.reels_with_plays}}.

findings.title: Recognition posts drew the most likes where likes could be compared
findings.text: At {{a.sig.brand}} and {{a.spa.brand}} the most-liked post marked an award from a treatment manufacturer ({{s.sig.likes}} and {{s.spa.likes}} likes). Denominator: {{a.sig.own_posts}} and {{a.spa.own_posts}} own posts; two accounts is too few to call this a pattern.

findings_takeaway: Follower count and reel count describe an account’s size and output; in this group, neither lined up with plays or likes per post.

blocks: In this window the account’s posts centred on women’s health.

Run the same topic as two reels with different openings and compare saves at seven days.
vit.takeaway: Ask your team to count direct messages per post as well as comments.

Paid boosting cannot be seen in public data.
Publish the next result as a reel and compare plays at seven days.
sig.takeaway: Test a second format before producing more of one.

blocks: Before this reel, the previous post was on {{a.las.before1}}, {{a.las.gap_days}} days earlier. The reason is not known from public data.
Publish weekly for eight weeks and compare profile visits.
las.takeaway: Ask your team whether any recent gap was planned.

blocks: {{a.spa.posts_in_window}} posts. The two posts before the window were on {{a.spa.before1}} and {{a.spa.before2}}.
With {{a.spa.own_posts}} posts, these counts cannot show which topic resonated.
Turn one consultation concern into a carousel and compare saves at seven days.
spa.takeaway: Measure saves seven days after posting against your last carousels at the same age.

patterns.title: Public conversation was thin everywhere
patterns.text: Median comments per own post were between {{p.min_median_comments}} and {{p.max_median_comments}}. The most-commented post had {{p.max_comments}} comments ({{p.max_comments_acct}}).

patterns.title: Treatment posts were the largest content type
patterns.text: {{p.t.treatment}} of {{p.own_posts}} own posts centred on a named treatment.

patterns_takeaway: A quiet comment section alone says little about how a post did.

tests.title: Steady schedule versus your recent pattern (finding 1)
tests.compare: eight weeks at a fixed number of posts per week against the eight weeks before.
tests.measure: profile visits and website link taps.

tests.title: Two openings for the same treatment reel (finding 2)
tests.measure: plays at seven days against your own reel median.

tests.title: Recognition posts against treatment explainers (finding 3)
tests.compare: pair each recognition post with an explainer in the same week.
